Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: No public scheme rulebook for BANTABA 2.0/Gamswitch found on operator or CBG sites; only marketing/overview pages were located (searched for 'BANTABA rulebook', 'Gamswitch rulebook', 'scheme rules', 'operating rules').

revision_notes: A single light-check search surfaced clearly authoritative Central Bank of The Gambia (CBG) sources, so the row was escalated from the fast to the full verification path. CBG publishes, freely downloadable without registration from cbg.gm: the Pricing Policy for the Payment, Settlement and Credit Reference Systems (approved 2013); the Operating Rules for the Cheque Imaging System/Automated Clearing House, covering participant access, system operations and settlement procedures; and a current List of Participants in the Payment System. No dedicated BANTABA 2.0/Gamswitch-specific rulebook was located, but the core CBG-regulated national payment system rules that BANTABA 2.0 operates under (BANTABA 2.0 is run by Gamswitch, wholly CBG-owned, settling via CBG's RTGS) are fully public. Score raised from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Yes - Fully Public).
revised_comments: The Central Bank of The Gambia publishes payment system governance documentation openly on its website without requiring registration, including the Pricing Policy for the Payment, Settlement and Credit Reference Systems (effective December 2013), the Operating Rules for the Cheque Imaging System/Automated Clearing House (covering participant access, technical and settlement procedures), and a current List of Participants in the Payment System. Together these cover participation, pricing, technical requirements and conduct for CBG-regulated payment systems, the infrastructure underpinning the BANTABA 2.0 instant payment switch operated by Gamswitch.

revised_comments: No confirmed, methodologically consistent estimate is available of the percentage of Gambian adults who have made a digital payment through the instant payment system in the past 90 days. Secondary aggregated estimates drawing on World Bank/IMF data suggest digital payment adoption in the region of 20-30% and mobile money account ownership below 20% as of 2024, but the underlying methodology of these figures could not be verified against a primary survey source.
